title: August and the Typewriter
premise: In 1911, on a monsoon-bound island trading post, fourteen-year-old Jonah Ashgrove discovers that the company that owns his indenture has been falsifying dive logs to hide the deaths of pearl divers, including his father. When the seasonal bridge closes and the evidence ship prepares to sail with the magistrate aboard, Jonah must carry the true ledgers past three checkpoints guarded by men who know his face. Betrayed by the one adult he trusts, he chooses truth over loyalty at the final checkpoint, and the ship sails without him — but not before the magistrate reads the pages. The novel ends with the company's agents arrested as the tide turns, and Jonah, indenture voided by scandal, walking the reopened bridge toward a mainland he has never seen.
about_author: Xanthe Vane is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing colonial shipping manifests in Southeast Asian port records. August and the Typewriter is her second novel, drawn from a salvaged ledger she once found sewn into the binding of an account book.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Things
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. He inventories what can be carried: a knife, a shell, his father's last letter. Establishes the trading post, his indenture to Halloway & Finch, and the divers' season ending in grief. Emotional beat: quiet endurance masking a boy learning that numbers can lie.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Kept
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Sent to fetch ink for the company clerk, he finds a second ledger hidden beneath the typewriter's carriage — real dive counts beside the false ones, deaths recorded as 'desertions.' His father's name appears three times. Emotional beat: the world tilts; grief becomes purpose.

chapters.title: Orders Come with the Rain
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The monsoon arrives early; the bridge closes for the season, stranding everyone. Manager Corliss announces the annual evidence shipment will sail with Magistrate Ellery aboard. Jonah realizes the false ledger is going to the mainland — and no one inside can testify against it. Emotional beat: claustrophobia and resolve.

chapters.title: Miss Okafor's Room Above the Chandlery
chapters.summary: Alternating POV begins. Adaeze Okafor, the clerk who typed the false entries under duress, has kept carbon copies of everything. She and Jonah form an uneasy alliance; she teaches him how documents speak. Emotional beat: two frightened people discovering they are each other's only witnesses.

chapters.title: Three Checkpoints
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. They map the route to the quay: the customs shed, the company gate, the gangway itself — each guarded by a man who knows Jonah's face. Adaeze sews the true ledger into the lining of a mail satchel. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into craft.

chapters.title: The Man Who Taught Him to Swim
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Sergeant Bray, his late father's friend and the customs officer at checkpoint one, catches Jonah loitering near the shed. Instead of turning him in, Bray warns him off — and Jonah realizes Bray suspects but cannot act. Emotional beat: loyalty as a trap disguised as kindness.

chapters.title: A Bargain at the Company Gate
chapters.summary: Adaeze's POV. Checkpoint two: Corliss himself offers Adaeze passage home and her freedom papers if she surrenders 'any irregular documents.' She lies beautifully, and hates how easily it comes. That night she finds her room searched. Emotional beat: the cost of survival measured in self-respect.

chapters.title: Bray's Choice
chapters.summary: Bray's POV, first time. He opens the mail satchel at checkpoint one out of duty, finds the ledger, and understands everything. He reseals it, then confronts Corliss privately and is bought off with a pension promise. Emotional beat: a good man choosing comfort, and knowing it.

chapters.title: The Gangway
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Checkpoint three: Bray, ashamed, stands aside — but Corliss intercepts Jonah at the gangway and demands the satchel. Jonah invokes the magistrate directly, claiming the mail is Crown property, gambling everything on procedure. Ellery descends the gangway to see for himself. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into audacity.

chapters.title: Morning Tide
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converge. Ellery reads the ledger on deck; arrests are made before the anchor lifts. Adaeze testifies; Bray confesses his silence. The bridge reopens days later, and Jonah crosses it carrying almost nothing — his father's letter, a shell, his own name. Emotional beat: justice arriving imperfectly, and a boy finally unmeasured.
